about: Built by data/build_sources.py from data/claims.json; one row per source cited on the page.

barnett2024.title: Seven Failure Points When Engineering a Retrieval Augmented Generation System
barnett2024.how: read PDF p.2 via pdfmd cache + pdftotext page check
barnett2024.use: Chunk size is a design choice with two failure modes: chunks that are too small cannot answer some questions, and chunks that are too long add noise. (Sec. 3 (RAG system overview), p. 2) | Barnett et al. name two families of chunking, heuristic and semantic, and ask for a systematic framework to compare them. (Sec. 6.1 Chunking and Embeddings, p. 4)

kamradt2024.title: 5 Levels Of Text Splitting (notebook)
kamradt2024.use: Kamradt's 'five levels' notebook orders splitters as character, recursive character, document-specific, semantic and agentic chunking; he calls it an unofficial list. (notebook cells 0, 27, 37, 77, 108) | Kamradt's semantic chunking embeds each sentence together with its neighbours (buffer_size=1) and cuts where the distance to the next window is above the 95th percentile. (notebook cells 83-84 and 100-102)

karpukhin2020.title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
karpukhin2020.how: read PDF p.4 via pdfmd cache + pdftotext page check
karpukhin2020.use: Dense Passage Retrieval split each Wikipedia article into disjoint 100-word blocks and used them as the retrieval unit. (Sec. 4.1 Wikipedia data pre-processing, p. 4)

langchain-code.title: LangChain text splitters: RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter (character.py), TextSplitter base (base.py), MarkdownHeaderTextSplitter (markdown.py)
langchain-code.use: The LangChain TextSplitter base class defaults to chunk_size 4000 and chunk_overlap 200 (measured by the length function, characters by default). (base.py, TextSplitter.__init__ (lines 64-65 at @1eeca8c)) | LangChain's RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter tries separators in order: blank line, newline, space, then single characters. (character.py, RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter.__init__ (@a2e53fd)) | LangChain's MarkdownHeaderTextSplitter splits on the Markdown headers you list and, by default, strips the header lines from the chunk text. (markdown.py, MarkdownHeaderTextSplitter.__init__ (@4e510a0))

gunther2024.title: Late Chunking: Contextual Chunk Embeddings Using Long-Context Embedding Models
gunther2024.how: read PDF p.14 via pdfmd cache + pdftotext page check
gunther2024.use: In the late-chunking experiments, a 16-token overlap on 256-token fixed chunks gave no clear retrieval advantage. (App. A.2, Table 6, p. 14) | Late chunking runs the whole document through a long-context embedding model first and only then mean-pools token embeddings inside each chunk span. (Abstract, p. 1; Algorithm 1, p. 5) | Averaged over 3 models and 4 BEIR datasets, late chunking improved nDCG@10 over naive chunking by 1.5 to 1.9 points absolute, depending on the boundary method. (Sec. 4.1, Table 2, pp. 7-8) | +3 more in claims.json

chroma2024.title: Evaluating Chunking Strategies for Retrieval
chroma2024.use: Chroma found that removing overlap raises token-level IoU, because IoU penalises redundant retrieved tokens. (Results, text after Table (text-embedding-3-large)) | Chroma reports that OpenAI Assistants' default (800 tokens, 400 overlap) gave slightly below-average recall and the lowest scores on the other metrics in its test. (Results, paragraph on OpenAI Assistants) | Chroma changed the recursive splitter's separators to add sentence punctuation, because the default separators often gave very short, poor chunks. (Chunking Algorithms: RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter) | +5 more in claims.json

duarte2024.title: LumberChunker: Long-Form Narrative Document Segmentation
duarte2024.how: read PDF p.4 via pdfmd cache + pdftotext page check
duarte2024.use: On 100 narrative books (GutenQA), recursive chunking was the strongest baseline after LumberChunker (DCG@20 54.72 vs 62.09). (Sec. 5.2, Table 1, p. 4) | On narrative books, proposition-level chunking scored low (DCG@20 46.19, below recursive and paragraph chunking), so its Wikipedia gains do not transfer to narrative text. (Table 1 and Sec. 5.2, p. 4) | LumberChunker gives an LLM a group of consecutive paragraphs (about 550 tokens works best) and asks where the content starts to shift; that paragraph starts the next chunk. (Sec. 3.1, Fig. 1-2, pp. 2-4) | +3 more in claims.json

llamaindex-code.title: LlamaIndex SentenceWindowNodeParser, HierarchicalNodeParser, AutoMergingRetriever (llama-index-core source)
llamaindex-code.use: LlamaIndex's SentenceWindowNodeParser makes one node per sentence and stores the 3 sentences on each side in metadata by default. (node_parser/text/sentence_window.py, DEFAULT_WINDOW_SIZE = 3 and window_size field) | LlamaIndex's HierarchicalNodeParser builds three levels of nodes by default, with chunk sizes 2048, 512 and 128 tokens. (node_parser/relational/hierarchical.py (@ad2efcd)) | LlamaIndex's AutoMergingRetriever replaces retrieved children by their parent when more than half of the parent's children are retrieved (simple_ratio_thresh=0.5). (retrievers/auto_merging_retriever.py (@26c7dc3))

qu2024.title: Is Semantic Chunking Worth the Computational Cost?
qu2024.how: read PDF pp.2-3 via pdfmd cache + pdftotext page check
qu2024.use: Qu et al. split every document into sentences with spaCy en_core_web_sm before any chunker grouped them; their fixed-size baseline counts sentences, not tokens. (Sec. 2 and Sec. 3, pp. 2-3) | Qu et al. tested a breakpoint semantic chunker (the four relative LangChain thresholds plus two absolute ones) and a clustering semantic chunker against fixed-size chunking. (Sec. 2, Fig. 1, p. 2) | Qu et al. conclude that the cost of semantic chunking is not justified by consistent gains; on non-synthetic documents fixed-size chunking often did better. (Abstract p. 1; Sec. 5 Conclusion, p. 4) | +3 more in claims.json

langchain-semantic-code.title: SemanticChunker (langchain_experimental/text_splitter.py)
langchain-semantic-code.how: read source code at commit f10d5c3
langchain-semantic-code.use: LangChain's SemanticChunker uses cosine distance (1 minus similarity) between consecutive buffered sentence windows, with defaults buffer_size=1 and a percentile threshold of 95. (text_splitter.py: combine_sentences, calculate_cosine_distances, BREAKPOINT_DEFAULTS (@f10d5c3)) | The SemanticChunker source credits Kamradt's notebook as the origin of the method. (text_splitter.py, SemanticChunker docstring (lines 102-105))

hearst1997.title: TextTiling: Segmenting Text into Multi-paragraph Subtopic Passages
hearst1997.how: unverified today: reused the j2 PDF search; not re-read (zsearch index was locked)
hearst1997.use: TextTiling (1997) is the older ancestor: it places boundaries where lexical similarity between adjacent blocks drops. (Hearst 1997 (j2 topic record j2-semantic-chunking); not verified)

merola2025.title: Reconstructing Context: Evaluating Advanced Chunking Strategies for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
merola2025.how: read PDF p.10 via pdfmd cache + pdftotext page check
merola2025.use: An independent 2025 replication found late chunking does not always beat early chunking: with BGE-M3 on NFCorpus and Stella-V5 on MS MARCO the early version won. (Sec. 5.2, p. 10) | An independent 2025 study found contextual retrieval keeps meaning better than late chunking but needs more compute (about 20 GB VRAM to contextualise long NFCorpus documents). (Abstract p. 1; Sec. 4, p. 7) | In the same study, contextualised chunks gained mainly when combined with BM25 rank fusion and a reranker, not with dense retrieval alone. (Sec. 5.1, p. 10) | +2 more in claims.json

anthropic2024.title: Introducing Contextual Retrieval
anthropic2024.use: Contextual retrieval asks an LLM to write a short context (usually 50-100 tokens) for each chunk and prepends it before embedding and BM25 indexing. (section 'Implementing Contextual Retrieval') | On the vendor's own datasets, contextual embeddings plus contextual BM25 cut the top-20 retrieval failure rate from 5.7% to 2.9% (49%), and 1.9% (67%) with reranking. (sections 'Performance improvements' and 'Further boosting performance with Reranking') | Anthropic estimates a one-time cost of $1.02 per million document tokens with prompt caching, assuming 800-token chunks and 8k-token documents. (section 'Using Prompt Caching to reduce the costs of Contextual Retrieval')

chen2023.title: Dense X Retrieval: What Retrieval Granularity Should We Use?
chen2023.how: read PDF pp.1,3 via pdfmd cache + pdftotext page check
chen2023.use: A proposition is an atomic, self-contained statement of one factoid; Dense X indexes Wikipedia as propositions instead of passages or sentences. (Abstract and Sec. 2, pp. 1, 3) | The Dense X Propositionizer prompt has four rules: split compound sentences, separate descriptive information about named entities, decontextualise (replace pronouns with full names), and output a JSON list of strings. (App., Figure 8 (prompt for GPT-4), p. 18) | Dense X did not run GPT-4 on the whole corpus: GPT-4 made a seed set from 42k passages, which was used to fine-tune a Flan-T5-large Propositionizer. (Sec. 2 'Parsing Passage to Propositions', p. 3) | +1 more in claims.json

zhao2024.title: Meta-Chunking: Learning Text Segmentation and Semantic Completion via Logical Perception
zhao2024.how: read PDF pp.3-4 via pdfmd cache + pdftotext page check
zhao2024.use: Meta-Chunking places boundaries at minima of per-sentence perplexity computed by a small LLM (Perplexity Chunking), or by a yes/no probability margin (Margin Sampling Chunking). (Sec. 3.1.1-3.1.2, Eq. 1-2, pp. 3-4)

nvidia2025.title: Finding the Best Chunking Strategy for Accurate AI Responses
nvidia2025.how: read blog (defuddle); vendor numbers, no paper
nvidia2025.use: In NVIDIA's vendor test on five document sets, page-level chunking had the highest average end-to-end accuracy (0.648) and lowest spread (SD 0.107); token chunks scored 0.603-0.645. (section 'Results', Figure 2 text) | NVIDIA found the best strategy changed even within one domain: FinanceBench best at 1,024 tokens, Earnings at 512 tokens, KG-RAG at page level. (Key findings, item 2)

shaukat2026.title: A Systematic Investigation of Document Chunking Strategies and Embedding Sensitivity
shaukat2026.how: read abstract only (PDF p.1); relevance graded by an LLM judge; method details not read
shaukat2026.use: A 2026 study of 36 methods in six domains found paragraph-group chunking best (mean nDCG@5 about 0.459) and fixed-size character chunking worst (below 0.244). (Abstract, p. 1; not verified)

sarthi2024.title: RAPTOR: Recursive Abstractive Processing for Tree-Organized Retrieval
sarthi2024.how: read PDF p.1 via pdfmd cache + pdftotext page check
sarthi2024.use: RAPTOR goes further than parent-child: it recursively embeds, clusters and summarises chunks into a tree and retrieves across levels (pointer only). (Abstract, p. 1)

edge2024.title: From Local to Global: A Graph RAG Approach to Query-Focused Summarization
edge2024.how: read PDF p.18 via pdfmd cache + pdftotext page check
edge2024.use: For graph extraction, GPT-4 found almost twice as many entity references in 600-token chunks as in 2400-token chunks (HotPotQA sample); GraphRAG uses self-reflection 'gleaning' to compensate. (App. A.1 Entity Extraction, Fig. 3, p. 18)

bhat2025.title: Rethinking Chunk Size For Long-Document Retrieval: A Multi-Dataset Analysis
bhat2025.how: read PDF pp.1,3-6 via pdfmd cache + pdftotext page check
bhat2025.use: Best fixed chunk size depends on the dataset: 64-128 tokens suit short factual answers, 512-1024 tokens suit answers that need broad context. (Abstract, p. 1; Sec. 4, Table 2) | The best chunk size also depends on the embedding model: Stella did better with larger chunks on long-document sets, Snowflake with smaller chunks. (Abstract, p. 1)

caspari2026.title: When Is Complex Chunking Worth It? A Multi-Objective Evaluation of Chunking Methods at Scale
caspari2026.how: read PDF pp.1,5 via pdfmd cache + pdftotext page check
caspari2026.use: A 2026 multi-objective study (8 methods, 2 scalable corpora, 3 embedders) found that expensive chunking methods rarely give consistent gains over simple ones. (Abstract p. 1; Sec. 5 Conclusion) | The same study argues chunking is a multi-objective choice: methods with similar retrieval scores differ in indexing throughput, query throughput and memory. (Abstract, p. 1)

databricks2025.title: The Ultimate Guide to Chunking Strategies for RAG Applications with Databricks
databricks2025.use: Databricks' guide lists six strategies (fixed, semantic, recursive, adaptive, context-enriched, AI-driven) and concludes there is no universal strategy. (sections 1-6 and Conclusion) | Databricks' 'semantic chunking' code example is actually RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter with separators; it uses no embeddings, unlike the Kamradt/LangChain method. (section 2 Semantic Chunking, code 'Example with LangChain (Recursive approach)') | Databricks recommends 200-500 tokens with 10-20% overlap for general text; it cites no measurement for this. (Best Practices item 2; not verified) | +1 more in claims.json

bytebytego2026.title: EP229: 8 Chunking strategies for RAG-based agents
bytebytego2026.how: read newsletter (defuddle); items 4, 5, 7 checked against kamradt2024, chen2023, gunther2024; no numbers in the post
bytebytego2026.use: ByteByteGo's list of 8 strategies (fixed, recursive, document-based, semantic, LLM-based propositions, agentic, late, hierarchical) matches the primary definitions we checked. (item list 1-8)

vecta2026.title: We Benchmarked 7 Chunking Strategies. Most 'Best Practice' Advice Was Wrong.
vecta2026.how: read the post; this is a method statement, not a measured number
vecta2026.use: Vecta's Reddit benchmark (50 papers, 30 synthetic questions, equal ~2,000-token context) reports recursive 512 best (accuracy 0.69) and semantic chunking at 0.54. (Results table 'The Big Picture'; not verified) | Vecta's semantic chunks averaged only 43 tokens at a 0.7 similarity threshold, which the authors admit was likely poorly tuned. (Finding 3 and Limitations; not verified) | Vecta equalised context by setting k = round(target tokens / average chunk tokens), so fine-grained methods got many more chunks (semantic k=46, propositions k=115). (section 'Equal Context Budget: Adaptive Retrieval k') | +1 more in claims.json
